prayerExcerpt.en-US: St. Augustine said, "I have never seen a compassionate and charitable man die a bad death."
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Santo Agostinho disse: "Nunca vi morrer de má morte um homem compassivo e caridoso."

meta.face: Two clearly different people, both Egyptians of the Roman age with warm olive-brown skin. Julian (left): a man of about forty-five with a KITE-SHAPED face, widest at high, angular cheekbones and narrowing both to a moderate forehead and to a small, firm chin — a straight nose with a narrow bridge, deep-set, kind hazel eyes, short, straight grey brows, a thin, gentle mouth; short, grey-streaked dark hair; a short grey-streaked beard trimmed to the line of the jaw. Basilissa (right): a woman of about thirty-five with a LONG, slender face and a long, graceful neck — a smooth, high forehead, a long, straight nose, large, dark, almond-shaped eyes set under long, dark, softly arched brows, gently hollowed cheeks, a small full mouth, a narrow, rounded chin; dark hair under the white veil; eyes lowered toward the tray.
meta.basis: The book's engraving shows the pair nursing in their hospital, Julian bearded in a plain tunic and Basilissa veiled with a tray of phials, which the card follows; Batoni's altarpiece at Santa Maria dei Monti (Wikipedia lead image) gives Basilissa in blue and Julian bearded with a palm. The Painter's Manual has a grey-haired St. Julian on 6 January among its martyrs, the Roman Martyrology's date for this pair; we take the grey only lightly because the identification is not certain. The structures are our choice.
